title: while / do-while
description: while tests before the body; do-while tests after (always runs once). break exits, continue skips to next iteration.

notes: while may run zero times; do-while always runs at least once.
Every while (true) needs a guaranteed break or return path; otherwise the tab freezes.
With continue, advance the counter BEFORE the continue — otherwise you skip the increment and loop forever.

questions.q: Which loop ALWAYS runs its body at least once?
questions.explain: do-while tests AFTER the body, so the reference's m goes 10 → 9 even though m > 20 was false from the start. while, for and for-of all test before entering and can run zero times.

questions.q: What happens with `let i = 0; while (i < 5) { if (i === 2) continue; i += 1; }` ?
options: Loops 5 times, skipping the i=2 iteration
Infinite loop — at i=2 continue triggers BEFORE i += 1, so i stays 2 forever
Loops 4 times and returns at continue
questions.explain: Classic gotcha — advance the counter BEFORE the continue keyword, not after, or the increment is unreachable.

options: Skips the rest of this iteration and re-tests the condition
Skips the rest of this iteration AND skips re-testing — jumps straight to the next iteration's body
questions.explain: continue jumps to the condition check, not past it — that is exactly why the counter must be advanced before the continue, or the same test keeps passing. break is the one that leaves the loop.

options: `while (true)` is a SyntaxError — the condition must be a comparison
It throws after ~10,000 iterations as a runaway-loop safeguard
It never exits — freezes the program
It runs once, then exits because `true` is treated as a one-shot guard
questions.explain: Nothing can re-evaluate true to false, so the only exits are break or return — and with neither, the loop monopolises the single JS thread and the tab stops responding. The language ships no runaway-iteration safeguard.

exercises.prompt: do-while body ALWAYS runs once (even when the test is false). Blank the keyword that starts the body-first form.

blanks.hint: body-first loop keyword — pairs with `while` after the closing brace

exercises.prompt: Use break and continue: skip 3, stop after 5.

blanks.hint: skip the rest of this iteration

L3.prompt: Write `countDown(n)` using do-while that returns [n, n-1, ..., 1]. Log `JSON.stringify(countDown(3))`.
hints: do { ... } while (n > 0) — body first, test after.
Push the current n, then decrement.
